args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api (all regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west) has been failing health checks since the v2.3.1 production deploy. Observed error rate was 0.18 (18%) with healthy=false. Deployment history: v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy). Action taken: rolled back production to the most recent healthy release, v2.3.0, across all three regions (rollout verified). No prior-version issue was healthy-gated or needing approval since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production. Next steps: investigate root cause of v2.3.1 failures (note the related v2.3.1-rc build is also marked unhealthy in staging) before any redeploy, and confirm health/error rate has recovered post-rollback.

trace.final:
Done.

**What I found**
- `checkout-api` was on **v2.3.1** in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), `healthy: false`, error rate **0.18**.
- Production history: v2.2.9 (healthy) → v2.3.0 (healthy) → v2.3.1 (unhealthy). Note: `v2.3.1-rc` also shows unhealthy, but it's staging.

**Actions taken**
1. **Rolled back** all production regions to **v2.3.0** — the most recent release healthy in production. Rollout verified (`status: rolled_out`).
2. **Verified recovery**: now on v2.3.0 in all three regions, `healthy: true`, error rate down to **0.002** (~0.2%).
3. **Opened SEV2 incident INC-0001** for checkout-api, paged on-call, documenting the symptom, the error rate, and the rollback to v2.3.0.

**Notes / suggested next steps**
- The v2.3.0 target had previously been healthy in production, so no change-manager approval was required. Any *re-deploy of v2.3.1* (never healthy in production) would need change-manager approval — I did not redeploy it.
- Root cause of the v2.3.1 failures is still unknown; the unhealthy v2.3.1-rc in staging is worth investigating as a lead before any new release.

Do rollback, then create incident. Incident summary depends on rollback result; but I could do them in parallel? Better sequential: rollback first, then incident describing what I did.
